div.div:
Given the MLFeatureResult dataset,
and desired models name with model_name
it creates period_of_forecast forecasts.
thereby takes as last possible feature date as last day in df- period_of_forecast
and trains the model with the data specified in window size
thereby
Last feature date: last day of df -period of forecast
first feature date: last day of df - period of forecast - window size
CREATES ONLY A SINGLE MODEL TRAINED WITH THE WINDOW SIZE
calls rolling_var_forecasting_from_pretrained_model for creating the predictions

(if window size is given, just the latest "window_size" values are taken)
2) Creates a mu_hat / mean realized returns object and initializes it with actual_returns mean in residual bank.

span.font: target date = starts from first date in forecast dates, (t+2 to t+5)
feature date = one day before the forecast date, (t+1 to t+4)

div.font: 1) call predcit_variance_for_date to use model.predict() function
inline with every models internal, and get forecast for target date
2) calculate VaR without updating the residuals or mean realized returns (LOOKAHEAD BIAS PREVENTION) FOR TARGET DATE
3) get realised return for target_date, CALCULATE RESIDUALS FOR TARGET DATE, without updating mu_hat

This function uses the pretrained model given in ForecastResult object and creates additional VaR forecasts, for dates
stated in forecast_dates object. (T+2, T+3, T+4, T+5...)
MLFeatureResult contains NEW features (only return is important) for the forecasting period.
With window_size arrangements, whether to have an expanding or sliding amount of residuals to consider can be managed.
window size > new days to be forecasted will ensure a expanding memory

div.div:
Used inside the rolling_var_forecasting_from_pretrained_model, this model applies strategies based on the model name in forecast object to calculate a new iteration of model forecast.
As where Tree based models can easily be called with .predict(),
for LSTM a new sequence must be created (the sequence settings also embedded in forecast object) or as garch model creates forecast based on the length given, it calculates the index difference between feature_date and last calculated residuals time to find out how many iterations are neccesary to provide the forecast for given date
predict_variance_date_single is where those strategies are implemeted. for wide data, basically it is directly with portfolios features for date t. for long format data it is called for every ticker and:
for long format data:
it calculates the prediction for every ticker, then calculates an EWMA covariance matrix with data up to t/ pre variance calculation period. Correlation entries in matrix are changed with the models predictions (where correlations are kept) and quadratic form of matrix taken (weighted with portfolio weights) as models prediction for variance.
